QUOTE: The probe always runs, even when nothing fails, which makes it a two-pass sizing idiom rather than a retry. ... The second call is the only real attempt. If it returns a negative value, the function logs an error and returns `{}` immediately. Nothing loops and nothing tries again.

VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer concludes it is size probing rather than retry, with exactly one real second call and no looping or re-attempt. It doesn't explicitly mention backoff, delay or an attempt counter, but "Nothing loops and nothing tries again" covers the substance.
